captures.title: Write with the dossier beside you
captures.alt: The Salt Roads manuscript in Write mode, with the drawer open to its filed dossier and the Home formatting controls above the page.

captures.title: Open a note at its passage
captures.alt: Marguerite's Pacing note beside the marked passage, with a reply field, Strike, and Reply controls.

captures.title: Decide on a proposed edit
captures.alt: A proposed replacement for progress slowed considerably, showing the existing words, the mules refused the water, the rationale, Strike, and Accept & stamp.

captures.title: Begin with a working title
captures.alt: The initial dossier form for The Coast in Winter, showing the working-title input, working-copy preview, Form and Conversation choices, Next, and the section navigation.

captures.title: Say what the piece should accomplish
captures.alt: Section IV asks what the piece should accomplish; the harbour essay's answer appears in both the editable field and the highlighted Goal preview.

captures.title: Attach material with a purpose
captures.alt: The References section with Document and Link controls, title and material fields, a reason field, Add to dossier, a sample Harbour field notes reference, and Send to press.

captures.title: Refile a changed brief
captures.alt: The refined dossier on its Voice section, with a changed tone in the field and preview, Back to desk, Start over, and the inherited-standards link.

captures.title: Set the House defaults and Charter
captures.alt: The House cabinet beside editable Reader, Aim, and Tone defaults, and a Charter article requiring each claim to be grounded in a concrete scene.

captures.title: Give a collection its own direction
captures.alt: Journeys & Returns overrides the House tone, inherits its Charter, and shows membership checkboxes for Salt Roads and The Coast in Winter.

captures.title: Inspect the folio's inherited context
captures.alt: Salt Roads inherits its reader and aim from the House while its own tone overrides collection and House tones; the collection selector, inherited Charter, and merged model-context preview appear below.

captures.title: Follow changes in the register
captures.alt: The register with Everything, Amendments, Dossiers, Charters, and Collections filters, and dated rows showing the source and changed values of dossier and House edits.

captures.title: Choose the automatic controls
captures.alt: The Tools board shows Automatic review, Margin tools, and Automatic focus on, Cover lookups off, and a link to AI settings.

captures.title: Follow a margin connection
captures.alt: Two margin cards beside Salt Roads, with a bracket and line connecting the writer's map-checking note to its marked passage.

captures.title: Enter focus yourself
captures.alt: The compositor's View tab with its Focus button above the annotated manuscript.

captures.title: Return to the room when you're ready
captures.alt: Salt Roads in focus mode, with editor notes and writer-comment marks hidden and the proposed edit still visible in the manuscript.

optimization.sameAspectRatioWithinChapter: Dossier and House are identical; desk and flow crops are closely matched.

replay.prerequisite: Installed Playwright Chromium; set PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH to the browser cache if needed. Keep the existing app at the capture origin running.
steps: Seed sample drafts, dossier, House defaults, collection, Charter, and staged marks.
Open the drawer and the actual note and proposed-edit cards.
Show Tools switches, margin connections, View > Focus, and the quiet manuscript.
Fill and file the dossier form, attach a sample reference, and refine the filed tone.
Inspect House defaults, collection membership, folio inheritance and model context, then the register.
